ptr.note: Allocator stored in pool->alloc (NULL selects av_buffer_alloc) and called later by av_buffer_pool_get, under the pool mutex, from any thread, until the pool is freed (possibly after av_buffer_pool_uninit). Each result must be NULL or a sole, writable reference whose AVBuffer data holds at least size bytes. pool_alloc_buffer copies the result's data/opaque/free into the BufferPoolEntry but leaves its AVBuffer flags_internal, so a result that is BUFFER_FLAG_REALLOCATABLE (av_buffer_realloc of an empty slot, or a buffer av_buffer_realloc's copy path made) hands out a first pool buffer that av_buffer_realloc resizes IN PLACE: av_realloc frees or shrinks the block the entry still records, which the pool later recycles (use after free) and frees again at flush (double free). The C contract does not forbid such a result. Rust: BufferPool::new passes NULL; custom allocators go through av_buffer_pool_init2 (BufferPool::with_allocator).

A fresh av_mallocz'd pool with an initialised mutex and refcount 1, the caller's reference, released by av_buffer_pool_uninit; NULL on allocation or mutex-init failure. Rust: adopted into BufferPoolBox = CBox<BufferPool, BufferPoolUninit>.
